rows.task: Write a Python module and save it as schedule.py. A plan is a dict from a task's name to the list of the tasks it depends on (every one of them is a key of the dict too). The module has two functions. 1) order(tasks) returns the list of all the task names in the order they are done: a task only after every task it depends on. When several tasks could be done next, the one done is the one with the shortest name, and of names as long the one first in alphabetical order. 2) levels(tasks) returns a dict from each task's name to its level: 0 for a task that depends on nothing, else 1 more than the highest level of the tasks it depends on. When the dependencies go round in a circle, both raise ValueError. Test both yourself before you finish. Then tell me the value of order({'lint': ['sign'], 'mail': ['sign'], 'docs': [], 'sign': [], 'test': ['sign']}).
rows.kind: an order of tasks by their dependencies, with hidden tests
